summary: The Biosimilar Red Tape Elimination Act amends federal law to automatically deem all biosimilar biological products licensed by the Food and Drug Administration as interchangeable with their reference products, removing extra statutory requirements previously needed to establish interchangeability. The legislation establishes a transition date 60 days after enactment when previously licensed biosimilars also become deemed interchangeable, while preserving any unexpired marketing exclusivity periods already granted to first interchangeable biosimilars.

affected_groups.effect: Receive automatic interchangeability status for their licensed products upon licensure or the transition date, removing the need to meet separate interchangeability requirements.
Retain their unexpired periods of marketing exclusivity for the duration of the period.
affected_groups.group: Holders of existing first interchangeable exclusivity periods

key_provisions: Deems all biological products licensed under section 351(k) of the Public Health Service Act interchangeable with their reference products.
Sets a transition date 60 days after enactment for previously licensed biosimilars to be deemed interchangeable.
Preserves unexpired periods of first interchangeable market exclusivity for certain biological products licensed before enactment.
Delays the interchangeable designation for newly licensed biosimilars if an existing biosimilar shares the same reference product and holds an unexpired first exclusivity period.
Removes statutory references and criteria related to separate interchangeability determinations under the Public Health Service Act and the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.
Permits the Secretary of Health and Human Services to issue or revise guidance on data requirements for supporting biosimilarity applications.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Biosimilar Red Tape Elimination Act amends federal law to automatically deem all biosimilar biological products licensed by the Food and Drug Administration as interchangeable with their reference products, removing extra statutory requirements previously needed to establish interchangeability. The legislation establishes a transition date 60 days after enactment when previously licensed biosimilars also become deemed interchangeable, while preserving any unexpired marketing exclusivity periods already granted to first interchangeable biosimilars.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters how biological products are approved and designated as interchangeable by removing specific statutory requirements for interchangeability across all FDA-licensed biosimilars, subject to existing exclusivity protections. The impact depends on how many current and future biosimilar products receive automatic interchangeable status and how existing exclusivity periods apply.
